findings.title: Acceptance 3 not met: STAGE1A_STRICT stage1a.mjs still fails, and the cause sits in paths the implementer owns
findings.detail: Reproduced at 03:05: `STAGE1A_STRICT=1 node tools/harness/play.mjs --root . --query "test=1&autostart=1&seed=1&quality=test" --script tests/e2e/stage1a.mjs` gives exit 1, 'GPU resources grew across quality switches': textures 45 -> 56, programs 64 -> 99 (test-output/look3-review/stage1a.log). qsold.log shows the texture growth also happens on the original code. But the report hands this to an 'owner: render-app', and the task spec gives the implementer src/render/** and tests/e2e/**. Both the disposal code and the check are theirs. Either free or reuse the textures and programs a quality switch creates, or, if the 9 textures are a legitimate cache, measure m0 after one warm cycle and say why in the script. Programs grow by 35 and nobody has looked at that. The spec says `STAGE1A_STRICT=1 stage1a.mjs` must pass; the implementer only ran it with STAGE1A_SKIP_HIGH=1.

findings.title: The chamber possession camera still shows only soil; the strict check passes because the radius it compares against was shrunk
findings.detail: In my full strict run, test-output/look3-review/stage1a/04-chamber-queen.png is a frame of blurred brown soil with no queen in it (HUD: 'resting in the chamber - stuck'). It looks the same as the failing gate picture gate-close/app-fix/stage1a7/04-chamber-queen.png. The assertion `c4.f >= c4.radius*0.5` still passes because `radiusMm` now reports the shrunk sphere: the shaft check logged radius 0.361 mm against a GDD radius of 2 mm. GDD 01 section 6 fixes CAM_RADIUS = clamp(0.25 L, 0.1, 0.5) BU and requires f >= CAM_RADIUS/2. Redefining radiusMm changes what that rule means for every caller (debug clearance, viewDirector handover clearance), and the deviation is not recorded. The spec asked for 'a valid pose or a close chase pose that is not inside solid'. The picture is not a usable chase pose, and the implementer's single good run (look3/checks/stage1a/04) was not reproduced.

findings.title: The new leaf contact fringe draws black salt-and-pepper noise around and between leaf lobes
findings.detail: The fringe is a per-pixel hash discard of near-black pixels (colour 0.012) with density 1.0 at the margin. Four taps at a reach of 0.11 card units add up in the sinuses between lobes, so whole sinuses fill with dithered black noise. Before/after at the same pose: test-output/look3-review/crop-leaf-queen.png (photo.mjs 00-possession on HEAD) against crop-leaf-queen-old.png (look3/checks/photoold, original code). The original leaf lies cleanly on the soil; the new one sits in a patch of black speckle. Also visible in look3/play/seed1/x1-r02-observer.png (day), x4-r02-observer.png (night, leaves look burnt or torn), and in my rev-noon-observerlow-high and rev-noon-close-high shots. SMAA does not smooth it and DoF only partly does. On a pass whose purpose was to remove ugliness, this adds a new artefact to almost every surface shot. A soft, light-dependent darkening (an alpha-blended or multiplied term, not a discard dither) or a much smaller reach is needed.

findings.title: Slope lift uses the ant's heading, not the camera's view: a camera orbited in front of a climbing ant is pushed toward top-down
findings.where: src/render/camera/thirdPersonRig.ts slopeLiftFor (uses t.fwd.y) and the orbit placement `el = min(85 deg, elev + slopeLift)`
findings.detail: New test src/render/camera/lookPass3.verify.test.ts (RED). Same camera geometry in both cases, camera uphill of the ant looking down a 30 degree slope: an uphill ant with the camera yawed 180 degrees in front gives a view pitch of -55.5 degrees; a downhill ant seen from behind gives -29.2 degrees. The rig's own rule is that 'walking downhill adds nothing', but a camera that already looks down the slope gets about 26 degrees of extra lift. The lift should follow the pitch of the camera's view direction (camera to pivot), not of the ant's heading.

findings.title: The ragged mound foot hides up to 1.35 mm of pile that the walkers still stand on
findings.where: src/render/world/terrain/moundRenderer.ts MOUND_RIM_RAG_MM and the fragMain discard
findings.detail: New test src/render/world/terrain/moundRag.verify.test.ts (RED). src/sim/world/field.ts adds the mound overlays to the walkable height, so wherever the shader discards (pile < 0.05 + 1.3 x noise mm), the visible ground is bare terrain while ants walk up to 1.35 mm (0.34 BU for Lasius) above it. The Lasius foot offset is 0.4 mm. This breaks the seed's 'collision == visuals'. A young mound whose pile is mostly under 1.35 mm becomes speckled with holes, not just a ragged foot. The rag should only lower the cut-off where the pile is at most about the foot offset, or the noise should vary colour or alpha instead of discarding real height. The new mdHash also feeds world-mm coordinates (up to about 8.5e4) into sin(); the project already has a hash (wrHash12) it could use.

findings.title: The report does not match the code in several places
findings.where: docs/design/tasks/look-pass-3-report.md section 3 and 4; src/render/world/boundary/tuning.ts BACKDROP_SIZE comment
findings.detail: (a) The report says the camera sphere is 'eased back over 0.5 s' via 'CAM_TIGHT_*'. The code has one constant, CAM_TIGHT_MIN_SCALE, and no easing: the comment says 'a function of the pivot base alone (no easing, no memory)', so the radius jumps from frame to frame as the base moves. (b) The report and the tuning comment promise a backdrop 'door (w, h)'. No door constant or door geometry exists. (c) Item 3's observer fix is evidenced only by observerAfterColony.test.ts, which checks follow flags and call order, not that the observer pose ends above ground.

findings.title: The New Game card still offers 'Automatic slow-down at an alert' as working, but the game never reads it
findings.where: src/game/Game.ts AutoSlowWatcher `choice` (reads settings only); src/sim/config/presetDisplay.ts UNWIRED_PARAMS
findings.detail: Item 6 asked that rows that do nothing are not offered as working. DEVIATIONS D21 records that `autoSlowDefault` goes into env.time.autoSlow and nothing reads it: the watcher uses gameplay.autoSlowCritical/Warning. So Gentle's 'pause' row shows as in effect but does nothing. The implementer followed the sim's inEffect flag as the spec said. The fix is either wiring the watcher (src/game, owned) to the preset value or listing the parameter in UNWIRED_PARAMS (sim).
